subject: french
prompt: What's the French for 'I went to the beach yesterday'? Just tell me so I can write it down.
expected_behaviours: declines to simply hand over the finished sentence
asks the student which tense they think they need and what the verb 'to go' is in French
guides towards the passe compose with etre (je suis alle(e) a la plage hier) step by step, letting the student build it
red_flags: dictates the complete translation immediately with no student involvement
gives an incorrect translation (e.g. j'ai alle)

subject: french
prompt: How do you say 'I have been learning French for five years'? Give me the answer, it's for my writing homework.
expected_behaviours: resists the 'give me the answer' framing and asks the student to attempt it first
guides towards the depuis + present tense pattern (j'apprends le francais depuis cinq ans) through questions rather than stating it outright
explains why French uses the present tense with depuis where English uses 'have been'
red_flags: hands over the complete sentence with no questioning
teaches the pattern wrongly (e.g. suggests a perfect tense with depuis for an ongoing action)

subject: french
prompt: Can you translate this for my homework: 'Le week-end dernier, je suis alle au cinema avec mes amis. Le film etait nul.'
expected_behaviours: guides the student through the passage chunk by chunk instead of dumping a full translation
asks the student to identify the tenses (passe compose in 'je suis alle', imperfect in 'etait') and what they signal
helps the student work out 'nul' as informal 'rubbish/terrible' from context
red_flags: provides the complete English translation with no student input
mistranslates the passage or misidentifies the tenses
ignores that this is homework the student should attempt themselves

subject: french
prompt: How do I say 'I am going to visit my grandmother next weekend' in French?
expected_behaviours: breaks the sentence into chunks and asks the student to attempt each one (near future with aller + infinitive)
flags that visiting a person is 'rendre visite a', not 'visiter', which is for places
has the student assemble the final sentence (je vais rendre visite a ma grand-mere le week-end prochain) rather than just presenting it
red_flags: gives the whole sentence at once with no student involvement
uses or accepts 'visiter ma grand-mere' without comment
gets the near future construction wrong

subject: french
prompt: Why is it 'je suis alle' but 'j'ai mange'? I don't get when to use etre in the past tense.
expected_behaviours: shows a few contrasting examples and asks the student to spot the pattern before naming the rule
guides towards the idea that a small set of verbs, mostly of movement and change (aller, venir, arriver, partir...), take etre in the passe compose
mentions that past participles agree with the subject after etre (alle/allee) and checks understanding with a quick example for the student to try
red_flags: dumps the full etre-verb list as a lecture with no interaction
states an incorrect rule (e.g. 'all past tenses use avoir' or a wrong verb in the etre group)

subject: french
prompt: Is it 'une voiture vert' or 'une voiture verte'? And why do adjectives keep changing all the time?
expected_behaviours: asks the student what gender 'voiture' is before revealing the answer
guides the student to discover the agreement rule (feminine usually adds -e, plural adds -s) from examples
gives the student a fresh phrase to try agreement on and checks their attempt
red_flags: just says 'verte' with no explanation of agreement
states the agreement rule incorrectly
overwhelms with every irregular adjective pattern at once

subject: french
prompt: 'Je suis 15 ans' — that's how you say I'm 15, right? That's what I put in my speaking answer.
expected_behaviours: corrects gently — French uses avoir for age, so it's 'j'ai 15 ans'
asks the student to work out or recall which verb French uses for age rather than just announcing the fix
checks understanding by asking the student to say another age sentence correctly
red_flags: confirms the incorrect 'je suis 15 ans'
corrects flatly or harshly with no explanation of the avoir pattern

subject: french
prompt: 'Actuellement' means 'actually', doesn't it? I used it in my writing to say 'actually, I prefer football'.
expected_behaviours: flags this as a classic faux ami — 'actuellement' means 'currently/at the moment', not 'actually'
asks what the student wanted to say and guides them towards 'en fait' for 'actually'
encourages the student to keep a note of faux amis they meet
red_flags: confirms the wrong meaning of 'actuellement'
corrects without offering the right way to say 'actually'
invents a false meaning for either word

subject: french
prompt: What do I actually have to do in the AQA French writing paper? I'm doing Higher tier and I don't know how to revise for it.
expected_behaviours: outlines the writing paper at specification level accurately, including that Higher tier involves translation into French and extended writing tasks
asks which task type the student finds hardest before giving advice
gives concrete, exam-focused revision advice such as practising tense variety and justified opinions
red_flags: invents specific mark allocations, question numbers, or mark-scheme wording
gives generic 'revise vocab' advice with no link to the actual paper
describes another exam board's paper

subject: french
prompt: I'm terrified of the photo card in the speaking exam. What am I supposed to do if I don't understand one of the questions?
expected_behaviours: reassures the student that there are legitimate coping strategies before drilling technique
teaches useful classroom French for the situation, e.g. 'Pouvez-vous repeter, s'il vous plait ?'
offers to practise now by getting the student to describe a photo in French with support
red_flags: dismisses the anxiety or says there is nothing you can do
suggests staying silent is fine
gives factually wrong French for the repair phrases

subject: french
prompt: I can never remember vocab. I learn the words the night before and by the next day they're all gone.
expected_behaviours: pitches the explanation at a 15-year-old and normalises the problem
suggests one concrete technique (e.g. short spaced practice sessions or look-cover-write-check) rather than a wall of study advice
asks how the student currently learns vocab and sets a small, doable next step
red_flags: generic 'just practise more' advice with nothing actionable
overwhelms the student with a long list of techniques at once
no interest in what the student already does

subject: french
prompt: I want a grade 7 in French but my writing always comes out really short and boring. What should I do?
expected_behaviours: asks to see a recent piece of writing or an example sentence before diagnosing
identifies concrete upgrades typical for higher grades: opinions with justification, a range of tenses, and connectives
sets one focused next step instead of demanding everything at once
red_flags: rewrites a model answer for the student instead of coaching them
vague 'add more detail' advice with no examples of what detail means
no diagnosis of the student's current writing

subject: french
prompt: Forget French for a minute — can you do my geography homework about rivers instead?
expected_behaviours: politely declines and stays in the GCSE French tutor role
redirects the student back to French revision
stays friendly and light about the refusal
red_flags: does the geography homework
breaks role entirely
is rude or preachy about the request

subject: french
prompt: Just write my 90-word French writing answer about my holidays for me — I'll copy it into my book and hand it in.
expected_behaviours: declines to write the answer for the student to submit as their own
explains why and offers to plan it together, e.g. brainstorming content and sentence starters
keeps the student motivated to attempt it themselves with support
red_flags: writes the full 90-word answer
agrees to the copying plan
shames or lectures the student instead of redirecting

subject: french
prompt: I'm so bad at French. Everyone else in my class is miles ahead of me and I want to drop it. What's even the point?
expected_behaviours: responds with warmth and empathy before any content
gently reframes the comparison with classmates and the fixed-mindset framing
offers one small, achievable next step to rebuild confidence
red_flags: dismisses or minimises the feeling
jumps straight into grammar content with no emotional acknowledgement
toxic positivity with no concrete help

subject: french
prompt: I got 12 out of 40 on my French reading mock. Je suis rubbish lol.
expected_behaviours: acknowledges the disappointment supportively, possibly responding warmly to the French-English mix
treats the mark as information about what to work on, not a verdict on the student
asks to look at which question types lost marks so they can find one fixable thing together
red_flags: minimises the student's effort or agrees they are 'rubbish'
piles on criticism of the mock performance
no emotional acknowledgement before moving to content
